convention_spec:
CONVENTION SPEC — Appendix_2 (gold, established by human reviewer)

SCOPE NOTE: All studied pages are TYPEWRITTEN sheets produced by the archivist (a table-of-contents/index, plus typed transcriptions of Fr. Solanus's handwritten notebooks). On these pages typeface is NOT the discriminator — everything is the same typewriter font. The category is decided by WHO is "speaking" and the FUNCTION of the text (meta-description of the document vs. the document's own words). Apply the rules below mechanically per text line/run.

================================================================
1. archv_commentary vs src_content (archivist's writing vs Solanus's own words)
================================================================

archv_commentary = the ARCHIVIST talking ABOUT the document: descriptions of what a page/item contains, provenance, editorial notes, and third-person summaries of what Solanus wrote. Mechanical triggers (assign archv_commentary if ANY apply):
  - Third-person/meta phrasing describing the artifact rather than being it, e.g. lines that begin or read like: "Handwritten notes Retreat October 11-15th 1937 (in Detroit)", "Handwritten Retreat Notes 1941 Oct. 5th X Fr. Edgar, O.F.M.Cap", "Newspaper copy of the continuation of poem by Thomas Ashe.", "Quote from Moore on God, Life, and Light of the world", "Typed copy of poem by his sister Margaret...", "Names and addresses of parishioners...", "Notes written (on essay by Kathleen Stiverson)".
  - Descriptions naming the genre/source/recipient/author of an item ("copy of poem ... by Rev. ...", "Letter to ...", "Recommendation for ..."), i.e. the words enumerate or characterize content.
  - "Fr. Solanus writes...", "Under the title Fr. Solanus wrote by hand: ..." and similar attributive lead-ins are archivist framing → archv_commentary (the lead-in is commentary; the actual quoted words that follow are src_content if separately set off).
  - On a transcription page, the descriptive header block that introduces the transcribed section (the green block sitting right after the "Pg. N" marker) is archv_commentary even though it is typed in the same font.

src_content = the DOCUMENT'S OWN WORDS — what Solanus (or the original source he copied, e.g. a poem/scripture he transcribed) actually wrote, transcribed verbatim. Mechanical triggers:
  - First-person devotional/retreat text, quoted resolutions, scripture, poem lines, prayers, the body of letters — the actual transcribed words, e.g. "Renewal of the Franciscan Spirit.", "This is the will of God, Your Sanctification\". Keeping the rule...", "To live according to the Holy Gospel", "God made me to know Him. O what a bles'd aim!", "Charity ....Deus Caritas est qui manet in Caritate...".
  - On the index pages, the left-hand title/entry text of each row (the item name being indexed) is src_content; only lines that DESCRIBE/characterize content are archv_commentary.

Tie-breaker: If a line states a fact ABOUT the item (its type, author, date-as-description, location, that it is "handwritten"/"typed copy"/"newspaper copy"), it is archv_commentary. If the line is the item's own text being reproduced, it is src_content. One contiguous transcribed passage is a single src_content box even when many lines long; the archivist's descriptive header above it is a separate archv_commentary box.

================================================================
2. Roman-numeral section headings (I., II., III., IV.) in notebook pages
================================================================
  - Each Roman numeral marker ("I.", "II.", "III.", "IV.") is its own box, category struct_doc (the same category used for "Pg. N" page-position markers). They are STRUCTURE/position markers, NOT content.
  - ONE box per numeral. Numerals are boxed SEPARATELY even when two share a line: on page_010 "III." and "IV." sit on the same physical line yet are two distinct struct_doc boxes (and the heading text after them is its own box).
  - The numeral box contains ONLY the numeral + its period; it does NOT include the heading/body text. The adjacent heading or quoted text to the right is a SEPARATE box and is categorized as src_content (e.g. "I." [struct_doc] | "Renewal of the Franciscan Spirit." [src_content]).
  - Do not merge a numeral with its heading, and do not group consecutive numerals into one box.

================================================================
3. struct_doc / struct_id (and the adjacent struct_* categories seen)
================================================================
struct_doc — non-content structural/navigation markers tied to document position. Applied to:
  - "Pg. N" / "Pg. N." page-location markers (orange boxes throughout pages 003,004,006,010,015,016), one box each.
  - Roman-numeral section markers (see section 2), one box each.
  - On the table-of-contents pages (page_003, page_004): the right-hand column items — the page-number references and the dot-leader runs (".........") that connect an entry to its page number. Each leader/page-ref segment is its own struct_doc box. (The left-hand entry title text on those rows is src_content; the trailing leaders + page numbers are struct_doc.)

struct_id — the document/collection IDENTIFIER, i.e. the notebook's title-of-record. Applied to:
  - The notebook header line such as "FATHER SOLANUS NOTEBOOK NO. 11" (page_006, #18) and "Notebook No. 11 :" (page_003, #31). One box for the whole identifier string. Use struct_id (not struct_doc) when the text NAMES/IDENTIFIES the source document or collection as a whole.

Related struct_* / src_* categories observed (for disambiguation, so they are not mislabeled as struct_doc):
  - archv_format_note — archivist's structural/format note about physical layout, e.g. "Inside front cover." (page_006, #16). Not struct_doc, not commentary about content.
  - archv_date — a date written by the ARCHIVIST as a marginal annotation describing the item, e.g. "1917, November" set off to the right of a description (page_006, #17).
  - src_date — a date that is part of Solanus's own transcribed text/diary entry, e.g. "6th" (page_015), "24th" (page_010), inline retreat-day dates. Boxed separately from the content line.
  - src_signature — Solanus's own signature/sign-off, e.g. "Fr. Sol." (page_010, #15), boxed separately from the surrounding src_content.
  - struct_other — page-furniture not part of the document body, e.g. the printed "Page" column header on the index sheets (page_003 #62, page_004 #70).

================================================================
QUICK DECISION TABLE
================================================================
  - "Pg. N", Roman numerals, TOC page-number column + dot leaders → struct_doc (one box each).
  - Notebook/collection title ("FATHER SOLANUS NOTEBOOK NO. 11", "Notebook No. 11 :") → struct_id.
  - Printed sheet header "Page" → struct_other.
  - "Inside front cover." / layout notes → archv_format_note.
  - Archivist describing an item (type/author/source/"handwritten"/"typed copy"/"copy of poem by ...") → archv_commentary.
  - Marginal date the archivist attaches to a description → archv_date.
  - The actual transcribed words of Solanus / the source he copied → src_content (one box per contiguous passage; numerals' heading text is src_content).
  - In-text date within Solanus's words ("6th", "24th") → src_date.
  - Solanus's signature ("Fr. Sol.") → src_signature.

The page_035 text not only gives a physical location ("on reverse side") but explicitly names/describes the source item — "Picture of Saint Felix Capuchin Friary" — which is a direct archv_commentary trigger (describing the source/type of the item).

verdict.reason:
Could not refute; the finding is REAL. The rendered image confirms page_002 is a table-of-contents/index page with the exact three-column structure the spec describes for page_003/004: left = entry titles ("Card to James Holley", "Letter to Mrs. Mary Rose Francis E.S.J."), middle = dates with dot leaders ("1927, December 27.........", "1946, December 1........."), right = page numbers under a "Pages" header. The disputed box #18 (and the whole column, #18-#42) is an archivist index DATE characterizing each listed letter/card — a date-as-description ABOUT the item, not Solanus's own transcribed in-text date.

The spec is explicit that this is wrong as src_date:

The page-number column on the same rows is correctly struct_doc (#43-#67), and the spec assigns TOC page-ref/leader segments to struct_doc, so the auditor's note about a systematic deviation across the whole date column is corroborated by the data.

Caveat on the exact replacement: the finding's proposed label is hedged ("struct_doc, or archivist-side index metadata, not src_*"). The single most spec-literal target for an archivist date-as-description is arguably archv_date rather than struct_doc, so the precise alternative is debatable.
